rationale.conceptual: The method is Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with Lennard-Jones potentials, Ewald summation, and flexible model parameterizations. While GCMC is an established technique, correctly implementing multiple force field variants, the fluctuation formula for heat, and interpreting sub-step behavior requires careful algorithmic translation and domain knowledge.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves at least 5 sequential stages (preparation, two sets of GCMC runs, average-structure simulations, isotherm assembly, heat computation) with many pressure points and model conditions. Orchestrating numerous GCMC runs with different input decks and handling of force-field parameters constitutes a non-trivial engineering effort.

difficulty.reasoning: GCMC adsorption simulations with flexible zeolite force fields, requiring careful implementation of established but multi-component methods. Multi-stage pipeline with many simulation conditions and post-processing.

compute_estimate.reasoning: GCMC simulations on a moderate supercell (~2000 atoms) are CPU-bound; no GPU required. Memory requirements are modest for a single-CPU run. Input data is limited to zeolite structure files and force field parameters.
